mission: Make it dramatically easier for an ordinary human with a meaningful vision to accomplish extraordinary things with AI without becoming an AI project manager.
human_intent: Execute the AppDeploy-targeted Smart Board baton against the latest main HEAD and make the current runtime target serve the exact canonical Hub source state that the project actually identifies.
naya_understanding: The AppDeploy target was ready, but its source mirror was pinned to an older checkpoint commit while current main had advanced. The highest-value surgical improvement available in the authorized runtime lane was to update the mirror's immutable GitHub source reference to the exact current main HEAD, preserving fail-closed canonical identity checks. This improves runtime provenance without creating a competing renderer or state system.

authority.human_authorization: Explicit continuation baton in current execution context
authority.execution_scope: Canonical NayaNET Hub AppDeploy source mirror

constraints: Preserve the canonical Smart Board architecture.
Do not create a competing renderer, state database, feed, shell, or continuation system.
Keep the mirror fail-closed on canonical source identity.
Do not promote READY to production proof without browser/runtime evidence.
Keep IMPLEMENTED, VERIFIED, RUNTIME_VERIFIED, and PRODUCTION_PROVEN distinct.
Leave exactly one executable next action.
plan: Resolve the actual latest main HEAD.
Inspect the canonical Smart Board React implementation and the AppDeploy source mirror.
Update the AppDeploy mirror to fetch the exact latest main canonical Hub HTML commit.
Deploy and inspect the resulting AppDeploy snapshot.
Record the provenance lesson and successor baton.

observations: The current React canonical Hub source includes AppShellV3, the canonical ten-item intelligence navigation, SmartFeedBoard, and Primary Intelligence integration.
The AppDeploy mirror initially pointed at older static Hub commit 65e5578d24369da8975bfaf2741ad433295dad84.
After the surgical source-reference update, AppDeploy snapshot 1789509766843 reported READY and its deployed src/main.ts was inspected directly.
The public URL could not be independently fetched by the web retrieval layer, so browser-level runtime acceptance remains unproven.
result: The AppDeploy canonical Hub source mirror now tracks the exact latest main commit instead of an older checkpoint, while retaining its fail-closed canonical identity guard. The deployment is ready and the deployed source reference was directly inspected.

value_cost_risk.value: Prevents a ready runtime target from silently serving stale canonical Hub source and makes runtime provenance mechanically inspectable.
value_cost_risk.cost: One surgical source-reference update and deployment.
value_cost_risk.risk: The AppDeploy URL still lacks independent browser-level acceptance evidence; the target is not promoted to production-proven.

lesson: A runtime target can be healthy and ready while still serving stale project state. Runtime provenance must bind the deployed source reference to an exact current canonical commit before runtime claims are meaningful.
memory: AppDeploy readiness does not prove source freshness.
The canonical runtime target must expose an immutable source commit reference that can be inspected directly.
Current React Hub architecture and the static source-mirror artifact are distinct surfaces; they must not be silently treated as equivalent.
Browser runtime acceptance remains a separate evidence boundary.

next_action.instruction: Reconcile the AppDeploy target with the actual canonical React Hub implementation, not merely the static HTML mirror, then deploy the smallest complete React artifact that preserves AppShellV3, SmartFeedBoard, Primary Intelligence, and the canonical ten-item navigation; verify desktop/mobile interaction where available and record exact source/runtime evidence.
